title: A demonstration of interval-censored survival analysis
relevance: The statistical framework our deliverable is named after but has never used: when subjects are assessed PERIODICALLY, the event is known only to have occurred between two visits, and that is exactly what an epoch-pair canopy series produces - 'this crown was present in 2013 and absent in 2016'. Carries the warning that decides whether our numbers are valid: assigning the event to the MIDPOINT or END of the interval is a known source of bias and invalid inference, and midpoint assignment is the obvious thing a canopy-change analysis would do without thinking. The Turnbull estimator handles it properly. Read before any per-crown loss date is analysed or plotted.

authors: Hilbert, D.R., Roman, L.A., Koeser, A.K., Vogt, J. & van Doorn, N.S.
title: Urban tree mortality: a literature review
relevance: Supplies the demographic priors our sample design has been guessing at: typical street-tree annual mortality of 3.5-5.1%, with reported ranges of 0.6-68.5% for cohort studies and 0-30% for repeated inventories of uneven-aged trees. That directly informs open question Q50, the discordant-pair rate that drives paired-sample precision - our Search 41 assumptions of 4%/1.4% and 6%/3.4% sit at the low end once a multi-year epoch gap is compounded. It also reframes the deliverable: per-crown validity intervals are a DEMOGRAPHIC product - survival, life tables, mortality curves - not only a mapping product, and this literature already has the vocabulary for it.
